land.text: France, the whole outline, under the Empire proclaimed on 2 December 1852

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Second French Empire row starts in 1853; the Republic's shape serves 1852.

land.text: France, the Republic proclaimed on 4 September 1870

successors.note: Cliopatria has no shape in 1870 for the Third Republic (its row starts 1871); Alsace and most of Lorraine, 'which became the Imperial Territory of Alsace-Lorraine', passed to Germany only by the Treaty of Frankfurt of 10 May 1871, after the Empire's end.

rulers.name: Napoleon III (Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte)
rulers.note: Infobox '1852-1870: Napoleon III'; Emile Ollivier headed the government 1869-1870 and Charles de Palikao in 1870.

keyframe_review.note: 629,631 km2, the same outline as the Republic's 1848 shape (France with the Antilles, Guiana, Reunion and French India). The page gives no area and no infobox comparison is possible; it records no territorial change between the Empire's proclamation on 2 December 1852 and the Crimean War of 1854-1856.

correction.text: France as in Cliopatria's 1856 shape without its three Crimean cells: the Crimean War ended with the Treaty of Paris signed on 30 March 1856

keyframe_review.note: 625,779 km2 for 1856-1859: 3,852 km2 below 1853. The shape gains three cells at 44 N 32-34 E (Crimea) and loses 13 cells of the 1853 shape (nine at Reunion, four in French India). The Crimea cells are the Allied war zone drawn as land: 'The Crimean campaign opened in September 1854', Sevastopol fell on 9 September 1855, 'The Treaty of Paris, signed on 30 March 1856, ended the war'. The page gives no date for the Allies' evacuation of the Crimea, so the end of any occupation is bridged. No page opened records a French loss of Reunion or French India; the drop is left standing and flagged in the notes.

644,663 km2 for 1860-1861: +18,884 km2 over 1856, 82 grid cells in the Alps (44-48 N, 4-8 E), 58 of them inside the gazetteer's Savoy and County of Nice regions. The Treaty of Turin was 'concluded between France and Piedmont-Sardinia on 24 March 1860' and 'the Duchy of Savoy and the County of Nice were annexed to France'; the page gives no area for either, so no infobox comparison is possible. Menton and Roquebrune (1861) are inside the shape's cells or too small to see.

correction.text: France without the 38 Mexican cells (Veracruz and the Gulf coast): French troops joined the Spanish at Veracruz on 7 January 1862 but Mexico stayed Mexican

keyframe_review.note: 655,548 km2: +10,885 km2 over 1860, 38 cells in Mexico. The page treats the Veracruz landing as an intervention, not an annexation: 'French and British troops joined them in January 1862'; the Mexican land is recorded as an occupation in the ledger (counterpart federated-republic-of-mexico), not as French territory.

correction.text: France as in Cliopatria's 1863 shape without its 92 Mexican cells (Veracruz, Puebla, Mexico City, the Yucatan coast), for 1863-1869; the French left Mexico in February-March 1867

keyframe_review.note: 671,292 km2 for 1863-1869: +15,744 km2 over 1862, 92 Mexican cells in all. Mexico City was occupied on 10 June 1863 ('Following the French occupation of Mexico City on 10 June 1863') and 'Bazaine evacuated Mexico City on 5 February 1867', the last troops embarked on 12 March 1867; the infobox runs the intervention 8 December 1861 - 21 June 1867. The shape therefore keeps Mexican land for 1867-1869 after the French had left, and treats an occupation as French land. The ledger carries the occupation by town.

correction.text: France as in the 1863 outline without Mexico: the whole of France until the Empire fell on 4 September 1870; the German-held frontier zone is in the ledger as a contest, not as lost land

keyframe_review.note: 565,811 km2: 105,481 km2 below 1863. The shape drops the 92 Mexican cells and 348 cells of north-east France (48-50 N, 2-8 E), which is the zone inside Cliopatria's German Empire 1871 shape: it draws the situation at the end of 1870 after the Empire had gone. The page dates the war's first action to 4 August 1870 (Wissembourg), Sedan to 1-2 September, 'By the next day, on 2 September, Napoleon III surrendered' and the provisional government to 4 September; it does not map the German-held zone, so only Alsace and Lorraine are named in the ledger. The land held by the Government of National Defence belongs to the Third Republic's dossier.

ledger.note: 2 December 1852: Napoleon III is proclaimed Emperor and the Second Empire replaces the Republic. Infobox 'Empire proclaimed: 2 December 1852'; capital Paris. The page gives no boundary; the region is the Republic's outline.

region.text: Rome, where the Empire 'kept French troops ... to protect the pope'

ledger.note: 2 December 1852 (dossier boundary, continuing from July 1849): the French garrison in Rome stays under the Empire, opened at the Empire's proclamation so that it joins the Second Republic's occupation_end of 1852/12 without a gap. The Roman Republic (1849) page: 'French soldiers propped up the papal administration in Rome until they were withdrawn' at the outbreak of the Franco-Prussian War in 1870; the Second French Empire page: Napoleon III 'kept French troops in Rome to protect the pope from the new Italian government'. [Reviewer eu-20-m, 2026-10-31: year 1853 -> 1852/12, confidence 1 -> 2, source moved to the Roman Republic page.]

region.text: Kalamita Bay and the siege lines at Sevastopol

ledger.note: September 1854: the Allies land in the Crimea. 'The Crimean campaign opened in September 1854'; all invading troops were ashore by 14 September 1854; France had declared war on 27 March 1854. Sevastopol 'finally fell on 9 September 1855, after a 337-day-long siege'.
30 March 1856: the Treaty of Paris ends the Crimean War. 'The Treaty of Paris, signed on 30 March 1856, ended the war.' The page gives no date for the Allied evacuation of the Crimea.

region.text: Lombardy, Austrian ground fought over in the war for Italy

ledger.note: 1859: France goes to war with Austria in Italy. 'In 1859, Napoleon led France to war with Austria over Italy.' The page gives the year only and names no battlefield; Lombardy is the zone the Austrian Empire dossier of this project records as lost to Sardinia in 1859.
1859: France is victorious. 'France was victorious and gained Savoy and Nice.' The page dates neither the armistice nor the peace; the Treaty of Turin of 24 March 1860 is the next event.

region.text: the Duchy of Savoy and the County of Nice

ledger.note: 24 March 1860: Sardinia cedes Savoy and Nice to France. The treaty was 'concluded between France and Piedmont-Sardinia on 24 March 1860' and 'the Duchy of Savoy and the County of Nice were annexed to France'; plebiscites 15-16 April (Nice) and 22-23 April (Savoy); 'France took formal possession of Nice and Savoy on 12 June 1860'.

2 February 1861: the Prince of Monaco renounces Menton and Roquebrune to France. Menton page: Menton 'was an exclave of the Principality of Monaco until the disputed French plebiscite of 1860 when it was added to France'; 'Napoleon III paid 4 million francs in compensation to the prince of Monaco, who renounced his rights in perpetuity on 2 February 1861'. The page also says the two towns had seceded from Monaco in 1848 ('In 1848, Menton, along with its neighbour Roquebrune, seceded from Monaco') and were administered by the House of Savoy for ten years, so the de facto passage to France came with the April 1860 plebiscite; confidence 2 for that reason. [Reviewer eu-20-m, 2026-10-31: source and confidence 1 -> 2 from the Menton page.]

7 January 1862: French troops land at Veracruz. 'On 14 December, Spanish general Juan Prim occupied Mexico's main port, Veracruz', and 'French and British troops joined them on 7 January 1862'. Infobox for the intervention: 8 December 1861 - 21 June 1867.

17 May 1863: Puebla surrenders to the French. 'The French arrived on 16 March and began the Siege of Puebla. The garrison agreed to surrender on 17 May.' The French had been beaten there on 5 May 1862.

10 June 1863: the French occupy Mexico City. 'Following the French occupation of Mexico City on 10 June 1863'; the Assembly invited Maximilian to the throne on 11 July 1863 and the executive became the Regency of the Mexican Empire.
12 November 1864: a French fleet arrives at Mazatlan. 'On 12 November 1864, de Kergrist's fleet arrived at Mazatlan.' In the north-west the French were 'largely confined to ports' by 1866.

29 March 1865: a French squadron lands at Guaymas. 'A French squadron landed several hundred men under Colonel Garnier on 29 March.' The year is the page's context (1865), not repeated in that sentence.
September 1866: the French leave Guaymas. 'The French withdrew from Guaymas in September.'

13 November 1866: the French complete the evacuation of Mazatlan. 'On 13 November, the French completed the evacuation of Mazatlan.' On 19 December 1866 'Napoleon III announced that all French troops would be withdrawn, ahead of prior schedule'.
February 1867: the French evacuate Veracruz. The port was left to the imperialist General Perez Gomez when the French evacuated in February 1867 (page); the day is not given.
5 February 1867: the French leave Mexico City. 'Bazaine evacuated Mexico City on 5 February 1867.'

12 March 1867 (bridged): the last French troops embark. 'Bazaine and the last French troops embarked for Toulon on 12 March.' The page says nothing of Puebla's end; the date is that of the general withdrawal.

1870: the French garrison leaves Rome. The Roman Republic page: 'French soldiers propped up the papal administration in Rome until they were withdrawn' and dates the withdrawal to the Franco-Prussian War of 1870, leading to the Italian capture of Rome; it gives no month.

region.text: Alsace and Lorraine: Wissembourg (4 August), Spicheren (5 August), Worth (6 August) and the Metz fortress

ledger.note: 4 August 1870: the first action of the war on French soil. 'The first action of the Franco-Prussian War took place on 4 August 1870'; 'The Battle of Spicheren on 5 August was the second of three critical French defeats'; Worth followed on 6 August; 'About 160,000 French soldiers were besieged in the fortress of Metz'. France had declared war on 19 July 1870 (the Empire page says 15 July).

region.text: Alsace and Lorraine: Wissembourg (4 August), Spicheren (5 August), Worth (6 August) and the Metz fortress

ledger.note: 4 September 1870: the Empire falls; the war goes on under the Republic. 'By the next day, on 2 September, Napoleon III surrendered and was taken prisoner'; 'On 4 September, Jules Favre, Leon Gambetta, and General Louis-Jules Trochu proclaimed a provisional government'. The contest does not end: the Third Republic dossier carries it to the armistice (26-28 January 1871) and the Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871).

region.text: France, the whole outline, under the Government of National Defence from 4 September 1870

ledger.note: 4 September 1870: the Second Empire ends and a republic is proclaimed in Paris. Infobox of the Empire page 'Republic proclaimed: 4 September 1870'; the Franco-Prussian page: a provisional government 'proclaimed' by Favre, Gambetta and Trochu, the Government of National Defense formed in Paris on 4 September.

wars.name: Crimean War

zones.text: the Allied landing at Kalamita Bay and the siege of Sevastopol

wars.outcome: The Allies took Sevastopol on 9 September 1855; the Treaty of Paris of 30 March 1856 ended the war and the Danubian principalities became largely independent Ottoman vassals.
wars.note: France declared war on Russia on 27 March 1854 (Britain 28 March). The page gives no date for the Allied evacuation of the Crimea; the belligerent list is the war's usual one, beyond France and Britain which the page names.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: 'France was victorious and gained Savoy and Nice' (page); Lombardy passed from Austria to Sardinia, which ceded Savoy and Nice by the Treaty of Turin of 24 March 1860.
wars.note: The page gives the year only ('In 1859, Napoleon led France to war with Austria over Italy'); the war's article was not opened (page budget). The Austrian Empire and Sardinia dossiers carry the dated campaigns.

wars.name: Second French intervention in Mexico

zones.text: Veracruz, Puebla, Mexico City and the ports of the north-west

wars.outcome: 'Mexican Republican victory' (infobox, 8 December 1861 - 21 June 1867): Maximilian's empire fell and the last French troops embarked on 12 March 1867.
wars.note: The page says the Orizaba agreements 'broke down' on 9 April, 'as France made increasingly clear that it intended to invade Mexico'; Spain's Prim had taken Veracruz on 14 December 1861. Maximilian's empire is the second-mexican-empire dossier of another batch.

wars.name: Franco-Prussian War
wars.outcome: The Empire fell on 4 September 1870 after Sedan; the Government of National Defence signed an armistice (26-28 January 1871) and the Treaty of Frankfurt on 10 May 1871, giving Germany 'most of Alsace and parts of Lorraine'.
wars.note: The Empire's part ends on 4 September 1870; the German side is given by its Cliopatria row (north-german-confederation), the page's German-state allies were not itemised in the part read.

certainty.note: Metropolitan France is drawn from treaty frontiers (the Savoy and Nice line of the Treaty of Turin, 24 March 1860). The Mexican occupation zone (1862-1867) and the Alsace-Lorraine front (August-September 1870) are moving fronts, soft.

notes: BUDGET. Five pages (Second French Empire, Treaty of Turin, French intervention in Mexico, Franco-Prussian War, Crimean War) plus the Roman Republic (1849) page opened for the Republic's dossier. NOT SETTLED: (1) Reunion and French India sit in the 1853-1855 shape (9 and 4 cells) and vanish from 1856 on with no loss on any page; verdicts leave the 1856-1869 shapes without them (the overseas group, french-africa and french-india, should say). (2) The 1870 shape: 348 French cells (north-east, 48-50 N 2-8 E) lie inside Cliopatria's German Empire 1871 shape, far more than Alsace-Lorraine; the Franco-Prussian page does not give an area or map the German-held zone, so only Alsace and Lorraine are named. Alsace-Lorraine as a German gain belongs to the German Empire and French Third Republic dossiers (1871). (3) The Mexican occupations are recorded town by town from the intervention page; the Mexican dossiers of this project list more places (Guadalajara, Oaxaca, Chihuahua, Monterrey) that this page gives with other dates, and the 1862 shape draws 38 Mexican cells that the page does not support as French. (4) Menton and Roquebrune (1861) are confidence 1; the Monaco dossier cites the Menton page; 'Menton' is not a place in the gazetteer (reported for the gazetteer agent). (5) The page dates the Empire's start 2 December 1852 although Cliopatria's row begins in 1853. (6) The Cambodian protectorate of 1863 ('established a protectorate in Cambodia (1863)') and Cochinchina (1861-1863, 'colonising experiments') are on the Empire page but belong to french-indochina (se-03) and the Khmer Empire row; New Caledonia (1853) is undated on the page; Senegal and Algeria have no dates there. Counterpart slugs without a file when written: roman-republic-1849 (Italian group), north-german-confederation (eu-20 other part), federated-republic-of-mexico and second-mexican-empire (am-08).
